doc.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010

title: Recording the first album live and fast
summary: She met the star sidemen mostly at one quick rehearsal; the album was made old school and live, a method she still uses.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Did you meet those musicians before the session?

I met them — well I had met some of them before just from being a musician and being around and stuff like that, but mostly it was at the rehearsal for the record. We had one quick little rehearsal. I mean we made that record like this [snaps fingers], I mean we made it so fast. It was very old school. That’s the way Joel liked to work. We did

everything live. I still work that way now because I learned it from him, that it’s better to just play for real and get a good performance. You know, that’s how I sort of grew up in the record making industry, was doing everything the old way.
